items.title: Derivation of First Equation of Motion By Graphical Method

source_refs.note: Derivation of First Equation of Motion By Graphical Method: a main subheading of 2.4 Equations of motion, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 28-28.

blocks.text: First equation of motion can be derived using velocity time graph for an object moving with initial velocity vi, final velocity vf and constant acceleration a.

Let the velocity of a body at point A is vi which changes to vf at point B in time interval t as shown in Fig.2.5. A perpendicular BD is drawn from point B to x-axis and another perpendicular BE from B on y-axis, such that

blocks.latex: OA = v_i = \text{Initial velocity of the body}
blocks.text_alt: OA = vi = Initial velocity of the body

blocks.latex: BD = v_f = \text{Final velocity of the body}
blocks.text_alt: BD = vf = Final velocity of the body

blocks.text: From the graph it can observed that

blocks.alt: Velocity-time graph. The straight line AB rises from A on the velocity axis (OA = vi) to B (BD = vf). Dashed lines run from E to B, from A to C (length t) and from B down through C to D on the time axis; a double arrow beside BD marks vf.
blocks.caption: Figure 2.5: Velocity-time graph (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 2.5).

blocks.text: The value of BC in above equation can be determined by taking the slope of line AB, Which is equal to acceleration a.
This is the first equation of motion.
